title: Japchae
subtitle: Korean glass noodles with beef and stir-fried vegetables
excerpt: Slippery sweet potato glass noodles are tossed with beef, spinach and carrot in a light soy and sesame dressing. Japchae is served at celebrations and everyday meals across Korea.
sourceNotes: Japchae was first created in 17th-century Korea as a royal court dish. Today it is a classic celebratory dish served at birthdays, Chuseok and Lunar New Year.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Each component can be cooked separately up to a day ahead. Toss together and warm through before serving.

content.text: Cook each ingredient separately in the wok, then toss everything together at the end. This keeps the textures distinct.

items.prepNote: soaked in cold water for 30 minutes, then drained

content.text: Mix the soy sauce, sesame oil and honey in a large bowl. Set aside.
Cook the soaked noodles in boiling water for 6 to 7 minutes until tender. Drain and scissors-cut into shorter lengths. Toss with 1 tablespoon of the dressing.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in the wok over high heat. Add the spinach and cook for 1 minute. Season lightly and set aside.
Add another tablespoon of oil. Stir-fry the carrot for 2 minutes. Set aside.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil. Stir-fry the beef with the garlic for 3 minutes until just cooked. Add the spring onion for the last 30 seconds.
Add the noodles and all the cooked vegetables to the wok. Pour over the remaining dressing.
Toss everything together over the heat for 2 minutes. Taste and season.

items.cause: They were not tossed with dressing immediately after draining.
items.fix: Dress the noodles while they are still warm to stop them sticking.

items.cause: The soy sauce varied in saltiness.
items.fix: Add more sesame oil and a squeeze of lime to balance.

items.cause: Sirloin was sliced too thick or the wok was not hot enough.
items.fix: Slice as thin as possible and use maximum heat.
